subject: ClearSignal — Post-call: forensic readiness & export process

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
To: Emma Larson <emma.larson@clearsignal.ai>, ClearSignal Security <security@clearsignal.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.inference>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: ClearSignal — Post-call: forensic readiness & export process

Hi Emma / Security team —

Thanks again for taking the call today — good discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: we covered Redwood's audit and activity records surface and how you might consume exports for forensic readiness and compliance.

Recap / asks from our side:
- SOC 2 status: where are you in the SOC 2 timeline (Type I / Type II / in progress)?
- Reg compliance: confirm HIPAA applicability (you mentioned PHI may be present in some workflows).
- Retention window target (e.g., 1 year / 7 years) and immutability requirements (WORM / write-once-needed?).
- Preferred export mechanism: push to customer S3, secure download, or API-based pull?
- A pseudonymized sample export would help us validate the pipeline. We can accept NDJSON or Parquet.

Attached: Redwood audit log capabilities overview (redwood_auditlog_capabilities_v1.pdf) and a short SOC 2 readiness checklist (soc2-readiness-summary.xlsx). Also, if you have a vendor security questionnaire, please attach — we can route to Priyom and Rishi for answers.

Proposed next steps / timeline:
1) You share any outstanding compliance requirements + your vendor security questionnaire (if not already) — by EOD Wed.
2) We deliver a small sample export (pseudonymized) and an export-runbook — by Fri.

From: Emma Larson <emma.larson@clearsignal.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
Cc: ClearSignal Security <security@clearsignal.ai>, Procurement <procurement@clearsignal.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ClearSignal — Post-call: forensic readiness & export process

Thanks Karthik — quick answers below and I've attached our VSQ (vendor security questionnaire).

- SOC 2: We completed SOC 2 Type I in Jan 2026; Type II in progress (expected Q4 2027).
- HIPAA: Yes, HIPAA applies for certain integrations where end-user data contains PHI.
- Retention: Regulatory guidance suggests we retain certain records for up to 7 years; for operational logs we typically keep 2 years by default.
- Immutability: For some audit scopes we need WORM-style storage or tamper-evident exports.
- Export format: Prefer NDJSON or Parquet; can accept encrypted tarball to our S3.

Request: can you confirm whether API logs include request/response bodies by default? We need to understand PII surface area prior to accepting sample data. Also, procurement will ask for estimated costs for automated exports to our S3 (daily/weekly).

Attached: vsq-clearsignal-20270301.pdf

Appreciate the quick turn. Happy to set a 30–45 minute technical deep dive once you send the sample export.

—Emma
Emma Larson
Director of Engineering (Security)
ClearSignal

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.inference>

Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ClearSignal — Post-call: forensic readiness & export process

Hi Emma — I'm Rishi from Redwood security; thanks for the clear notes. Short technical answers and proposed export options below.

What we capture (high level):
- Admin/activity logs: user provisioning actions, role/permission changes, console admin actions, service account operations, with timestamp, actor, target, and outcome.
- API access logs: request metadata (API key id, endpoint, headers, request size, response time, status). By default we do NOT persist full customer payloads or model outputs in plaintext in the API logs; any sensitive content is protected and redacted per our data minimization policies.
- Model invocation traces: token counts, latency metrics, model version IDs, and kv-cache usage; payloads are only kept if customers opt-in for debugging (we lock that behind an explicit setting).

Exportability & formats:
- Exports supported: NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON), Parquet (columnar), and gzipped JSON tarball. We can push nightly exports to a customer-managed S3 bucket (AES-256 server-side encryption and optional client-side encryption).
- Ad-hoc exports: we can produce on-request exports within 48 hours for standard datasets; for very large exports (>10TB) lead time may be longer and we propose an ETL runbook.

Immutability & chain-of-custody:
- We support WORM-compatible exports by writing directly to a customer S3 bucket with object-lock enabled (legal hold / retention periods).
- Each export includes a manifest with file-level SHA-256 checksums and a signed metadata file. We also produce a basic audit manifest that lists sequence numbers and export timestamps to assist forensic reconciliation.

PII handling / pseudonymization:
- For sample exports we can provide pseudonymized records (stable hashed IDs, removal of direct identifiers) and a short mapping procedure if you need token-level re-identification under contract.

Next steps I suggest from a security delivery POV:
1) We'll prepare a pseudonymized NDJSON sample (~1000 records) and an export runbook.
2) We'll include instructions for enabling object-lock on your S3 target and a small script for verification (checksum validation).
3) Schedule a 45-minute technical deep dive with Hannah + Priyom + your infra lead to walk the export, retention, and immutability controls.

Attachments: vsq-sample-export.ndjson (pseudonymized sample), redwood_auditlog_capabilities_v1.pdf (reference)

If that works I'll kick off the sample creation this morning and share the link to the sample S3 staging location.

—Rishi Malhotra
Security Lead, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.inference

Looking forward to the deep dive.
